How much does fence installation cost?

A new fence around the yard — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$1,700–$4,000

$10–$20 per linear foot for wood, installed

Bay Area: $24 per linear foot on average — a typical 150-ft backyard fence runs about $3,600.

Why quotes run $6 to $50 per foot

Material
The whole job in one choice: chain link $5–$40/ft, wood $10–$20, vinyl $20–$25, aluminum $20–$30, wrought iron $20–$35, composite $15–$45.
Length & height
Price is per linear foot, so the yard's perimeter is the budget. Taller fences need more material — a 6-ft privacy fence costs more per foot than a 4-ft picket.
Old fence removal
Tearing down the old fence runs $4–$10 per linear foot — roughly $600–$1,500 for a 150-ft fence.
Terrain & extras
Sloped yards need leveling ($1,000–$4,000 in San Francisco). Gates, permits, and tree or root removal stack on top.
Material

Wood or vinyl

Wood
$10–$20 per ft

The classic: affordable, looks great, takes stain. Needs restaining every few years or it grays and rots. Most homes pick this.

Vinyl
$20–$25 per ft

Costs more upfront, then nearly nothing — no staining, no rot. Looks like plastic up close, which bothers some people.

Bottom line: wood for the classic look at the lowest price; vinyl if you'd rather pay once than maintain forever.

Common questions

How long does fence installation take?

One to three days for a typical backyard. Sloped terrain, old fence removal, or custom gates add time.

Do I need a permit for a fence?

Often yes — most cities cap residential fence height (usually 6 ft in back, 4 ft in front) and some require permits. Check before you dig.

How long does a wood fence last?

Decades with regular staining and prompt repairs; much less if you ignore it. That's the maintenance bargain you're signing up for.

Should the fence face in or out?

The finished side faces the neighbors — it's customary and often required by local rules. The rails go on your side.

Every yard prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on the material, the footage, and local labor rates. Take a photo of your yard in Brightglow for an estimate on the actual job, and to compare local pros who've done the same work.
